neighbours.label: words that state a mutual, reciprocal relation among several things (each other, interrelated, interconnected, coordination)
fire: In this model, diet, sleep, and stress are deeply intertwined and affect one another.
The two economies are mutually dependent on shared trade routes.
During the show the dancers must coordinate their steps with each other.
Climate, soil, and crops are closely interrelated in every farming region.
Because these networks are interconnected, a failure spreads quickly.
The two sisters supported each other through the hard winter.
Over time prices and wages tend to influence one another.
Inside the clock, the gears interlock so that each wheel drives its neighbor.
quiet: In this model, diet, sleep, and stress are measured separately each week.
The two economies are growing slowly despite new trade routes.
Before the show the dancers must memorize their steps in the studio.
Climate, soil, and crops are recorded each year in every farming region.
Because these networks are expensive, upgrades happen slowly.
The two sisters planted tomatoes through the long summer.
Over time prices and wages tend to rise in most countries.
Inside the clock, the gears are made of brass and polished by hand.
